clue.text: Express one's frustration on Bill's arrival

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a bill is an advert, abbreviated AD; the 's is read as 'has'
to vent is to let out pent-up feelings

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off irritably about the bill landing on the doormat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests an invoice, but the sense needed is an advert; 'on' places the frustration word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is a coming or arrival, especially of something important.

clue.text: Stroke requiring doctor to interrupt party turn

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the doctor goes inside

parts.note: a do is a party
milk or eggs that turn go off, or addle
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A medical emergency: the doctor interrupts the party's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests a seizure; it is a swimming stroke. GP is the British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog paddle is a simple swimming stroke imitating a dog in water.

clue.text: Promote cultivation of vegetable Great Britain's neglected

indicators.note: cultivation works the soil over, so the letters are reworked
neglected means those letters are left out of the mixture

parts.note: GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: Encourage growing greens, which Britain has ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' drops G and B from VEGETABLE; 'cultivation of' rearranges the remaining VEETALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote someone is to raise them to a higher rank, which is to elevate them.

clue.text: Light fire, as an alternative to central heating, to raise temperature

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a letter lifts it to the top

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Instead of switching on the heating, light a fire to warm the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' puts T above OR and CH in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is to set fire to it deliberately.

clue.text: Line was possibly crossed by this woman

indicators.note: crossed by means the scrambled letters are spanned on both sides by the pronoun

parts.note: a woman referred to as 'this woman' gives the pronoun her

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of was may be arranged in another order

explanation.surface: A rope or boundary was apparently stepped over by a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line was possibly crossed' reads like a rule being broken; 'possibly' gives AWS and 'crossed by' wraps the pronoun round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship, so a kind of line.

clue.text: Perhaps skinhead's beginning to sing heartily when drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
beginning to picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A skinhead starts singing loudly after a few pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a person; it is a haircut, and 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead is a closely shaved haircut, one example of a hairstyle.

clue.text: Prodigal son first to talk about breaking regressive law

indicators.note: breaking means splitting into the reversed law
regressive means going backwards, so law is read from the end

parts.note: the word law taken as written

indicators.note: first to picks out the opening letter of talk

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: The biblical prodigal son is first to discuss breaking a backward law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son' looks part of the definition but gives S. 'regressive' gives WAL, and 'breaking' splits that open.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal is a spendthrift who squanders money, the same as a wastrel.

clue.text: Uplift connected with trimming of wings

indicators.note: the wings are the two outer letters, which are clipped off

parts.note: related means connected with

explanation.surface: A feeling of lift linked to clipping a bird's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimming of wings' cuts R and D from the ends of RELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To uplift is to raise someone's spirits, which is to make them elated.

clue.text: When you're wobbly and about to snap, it helps to take drugs — lots of drugs!

definitions.text: When you're wobbly and about to snap, it helps

parts.note: to trip is to take hallucinogenic drugs
OD, an overdose, is too much of a drug

explanation.surface: When shaky and close to breaking down, drugs (and lots of them) seem to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' reads as losing your temper; it is taking a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged stand steadies a camera, so a shaky photographer is helped to take a picture.

clue.text: Repressed writer returned to couch

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: to couch an idea is to put it into words

explanation.surface: An inhibited author goes back to the psychoanalyst's sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couch' looks like a sofa; it is a verb meaning to express.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are pent-up are held in and not released, which is to say repressed.

clue.text: Heel of shoe beginning to get scratched

indicators.note: the opening letter of the shoe word is scratched out, struck off

parts.note: a brogue is a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations

explanation.surface: The heel of someone's shoe has started to get scuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' looks like part of the shoe, but it is the definition: a cad. 'beginning to get scratched' removes the B from BROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible, dishonourable man, a synonym of rogue.

clue.text: Bring back means of controlling condition

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse
a state is a condition, as in 'a state of repair'

explanation.surface: Reintroduce a method of keeping some situation under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former position, so to bring back.

clue.text: Exothermic reaction making asps rear then hop

indicators.note: making signals that the following letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A burst of heat as snakes rear up and then hop away.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of 'asps rear then hop' rearrange to the answer; 'making' is the signal. The asps fit the theme: the setter is Serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a firework demonstration where burning mercury thiocyanate gives off heat and grows a snaking column of ash.

clue.text: Place to avoid: it's surrounded by uninhabited cowboy country

parts.note: to dodge is to avoid

indicators.note: 's is 'is', so it is surrounded by the two outer letters
uninhabited means emptied of its inside letters, leaving just the ends

explanation.surface: A spot to steer clear of, ringed by empty cowboy country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uninhabited' leaves just the outer letters, which ''s surrounded by' wraps round 'it'. 'cowboy' is colour: Dodge City, Kansas, was a famous Wild West cattle town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodge City is a town in Kansas, a real place famous from cowboy history.

clue.text: Prompt I had to repeat, covering actor with confusion

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the jumbled actor goes inside
to repeat means the shortened phrase appears twice

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, written ID

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cue that I had to say again, leaving an actor confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with confusion' turns ACTOR into OTCAR, which the doubled ID covers.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot card is a cue card held off camera to prompt a presenter.

clue.text: Enthusiastically take on board young boxer from Hollywood?

indicators.note: from places the young dog as coming out of the place, the place first

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, abbreviated LA
a boxer is a dog breed, so its young is a pup

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly signs up a promising young fighter out of Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' wants to be a fighter; it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up something is an idiom for accepting it eagerly, like a pet drinking greedily.

clue.text: Dean mixed up with prior's fate

definitions.note: here a verb: to destine in advance

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dean entangled with a prior's destiny in some monastery intrigue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fate' is a verb here, to decide beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To fate something is to destine it, which is to settle it in advance.

clue.text: Struck by joint announcement of poverty

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word for poverty is given as heard

parts.note: poverty is need or want

explanation.surface: Hit by a joint statement declaring hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' reads as shared, as in a joint statement; it is the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: To be struck with the knee is to be hit with that leg joint.

clue.text: One supplying smack and ecstasy risks getting beaten up

indicators.note: beaten up means knocked about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug dealer offering heroin and ecstasy risks being attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' reads as heroin, matching the drug-dealing surface; it is a loud kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a noisy kiss, so the one giving it is someone who kisses.

clue.text: Most profound scourge of several rivers in Great Britain

parts.note: the Dee is the name of rivers in Wales, England and Scotland
a pest is a plague or scourge

explanation.surface: The deepest problem plaguing several British rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee names several British rivers, including ones in Aberdeenshire and on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest is the superlative of deep, meaning most profound.

clue.text: Best not to start by getting into it really seriously

indicators.note: by means beside, so the shortened word sits next to the earning

parts.note: being into something means being keen on it, which is in
getting money is earning it

indicators.note: not to start means the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Advice that it is better not to begin, once really committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start' turns BEST into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in earnest is to do it with sincere, serious intent.

clue.text: Sacked very old supporting artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly artist lost their job, propped up by a very old patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' suggests fired; it means plundered.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacked city has been looted and laid waste, that is, ravaged.

clue.text: Hear about death happening

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for death goes inside

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
death is one's end

explanation.surface: Listen out for news of a recent death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like listening; it is a court hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening is slang for fashionable, as is trendy.

clue.text: Writer put minimum of effort into transposed line that ends as it started

definitions.text: line that ends as it started

parts.note: the writer is this puzzle's setter, Serpent

indicators.note: put signals placing a letter somewhere
into says where the letter is placed: inside the other word

parts.note: transposed means turned round, in inverse order

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest portion, its first letter

explanation.surface: An author makes very little effort over a line rearranged to finish as it began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... into' places E inside INVERSE. 'Writer' is Serpent, the setter of this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpentine verse is a line of poetry beginning and ending with the same word, like a snake biting its tail.

clue.text: Dig out of bed with tip of spade and rake over

indicators.note: over means covering, so the rake word goes round the letter

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a rake

indicators.note: the tip is the first letter

explanation.surface: Turn over the bed in the garden with a spade and rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' and 'bed' suggest gardening; 'Dig out of bed' means get someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to wake them and get them up.

clue.text: I left without desire to score

parts.note: no means none of, without, as in 'no money'

indicators.note: left means departed, so that letter goes

parts.note: an itch is a craving or desire

explanation.surface: I've gone without the urge to score a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes I from ITCH, leaving TCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To notch is to score or achieve, as in notching up a win.

clue.text: Lavish underground system once operated with everything moving ahead of time

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.text: with everything moving ahead of time
indicators.note: every other letter is moved ahead of the letter for time, leaving it last

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway
operated means ran, as a machine or business

explanation.surface: An extravagant former underground network, with all its trains running early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with everything moving ahead of time' takes the T of TUBERAN to the end: UBERANT. The Tube is London's underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish and exuberant both describe profuse, extravagant abundance.

clue.text: Group's opening duo accompanied by piano

indicators.note: the opening duo is the first two letters of the word

parts.note: and joins one thing with another, accompanying it

explanation.surface: A band's opening pair, backed by a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' looks like an accompaniment; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is a large piano with a horizontal frame, as on a concert stage.

clue.text: Five years spent addressing packages

indicators.note: packages means contains, so the answer is wrapped inside these words

explanation.surface: Half a decade wasted writing labels on parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packages' looks like parcels; it is a verb: holds within.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a group of five, here a period of five years.

clue.text: Severe punishment greeting sound of bell

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
ding is the noise a bell makes

explanation.surface: A harsh penalty announced by a hello and a bell ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a thrashing or beating, so a harsh punishment.
